subject.title: Device identity generation should not depend on browser Secure Context — breaks HTTP reverse-proxy deployments

question: Should OpenClaw support persistent Control UI browser device identity when the UI is served over non-localhost plain HTTP?
rationale: Current code and docs intentionally reject remote device-less Control UI sessions to preserve the secure-context/MitM boundary; removing the gate is a product/security policy choice, not a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Keep remote HTTP rejected
options.body: Retain the current secure-context requirement and focus on warnings, loopback/Tailscale guidance, and trusted-proxy/break-glass recovery paths.

options.title: Add explicit opt-in support
options.body: Allow remote plaintext browser identity only behind a clearly named dangerous/operator-controlled policy with docs, audit warning, and focused upgrade/security tests.

options.title: Allow identity unconditionally
options.body: Replace the WebCrypto digest dependency and always attempt browser identity, accepting the changed trust boundary for LAN HTTP deployments.

recommendation.title: Keep remote HTTP rejected
recommendation.body: Retain the current secure-context requirement and focus on warnings, loopback/Tailscale guidance, and trusted-proxy/break-glass recovery paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Current main blame and prior review context point to recent ownership of the Control UI/gateway identity boundary.
